title: Restriction of scalars and extension of scalars along isomorphisms
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided monoidal closed category with equalizers and coequalizers in which
tensoring on either side preserves colimits, and let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
R & \xrightarrow{\ \varphi\ } & S\\
{\scriptstyle a}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle b}\\
R' & \xrightarrow{\ \psi\ } & S'
\end{array}
$$

be a commutative square ($\psi\circ a=b\circ\varphi$) of morphisms of monoid objects, with $R$,
$S$ commutative and $a$, $b$ isomorphisms. With $\operatorname{Res}$, $\operatorname{Ext}$ as in
[sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], there is a natural isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Res}_\psi\circ\operatorname{Ext}_b\;\cong\;\operatorname{Ext}_a\circ
\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\colon\Mod_S(\mathcal C)\longrightarrow\Mod_{R'}(\mathcal C).
$$

proof.text: Apply clause 5 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] to $b\colon S\to S'$ and to $a\colon R\to R'$. The hypotheses of its clauses 2 and 3 hold by the assumptions on $\mathcal C$; the source monoids $S$ and $R$ are commutative and both maps are invertible. This gives natural isomorphisms $e_b\colon\operatorname{Ext}_b\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{b^{-1}}$ and $e_a\colon\operatorname{Ext}_a\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{a^{-1}}$. Thus applying $\operatorname{Res}_\psi$ to $e_b$ compares the left side of the desired isomorphism with $\operatorname{Res}_\psi\circ\operatorname{Res}_{b^{-1}}$, while evaluating $e_a$ on $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ compares the right side with $\operatorname{Res}_{a^{-1}}\circ\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$. These four functors all have source $\Mod_S(\mathcal C)$ and target $\Mod_{R'}(\mathcal C)$.

source.place: First sentence: extension along each of the two isomorphisms is restriction along its inverse.

proof.text: Precompose $\psi\circ a=b\circ\varphi$ by $a^{-1}$ and postcompose by $b^{-1}$. Associativity and the two inverse identities give the equality $h\colon b^{-1}\circ\psi=\varphi\circ a^{-1}$ of morphisms $R'\to S$. Neither $\varphi$ nor $\psi$ needs to be invertible.

source.place: Last clause: derive the inverse-square equality from commutativity.

proof.text: For an $S$-module $M$ with action $\gamma_M$, [def-sfb-modobj-restriction] gives the action of $\operatorname{Res}_\psi\operatorname{Res}_{b^{-1}}M$ as $\gamma_M\circ(b^{-1}\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)\circ(\psi\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)=\gamma_M\circ((b^{-1}\circ\psi)\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)$. The action of $\operatorname{Res}_{a^{-1}}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi M$ is $\gamma_M\circ(\varphi\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)\circ(a^{-1}\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)=\gamma_M\circ((\varphi\circ a^{-1})\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)$. Tensor functoriality gives these equalities, and $h$ from step 2 identifies the final actions. By the module-morphism definition in [det-def-sfb-module-objects-definition], the underlying identity $\mathrm{id}_M$ and its inverse are therefore $R'$-linear. They define an isomorphism $k_M$ from the first restricted module to the second. Both composite restrictions leave every underlying arrow $u\colon M\to N$ unchanged, so naturality reads $u\circ\mathrm{id}_M=\mathrm{id}_N\circ u$. Hence the $k_M$ form a natural isomorphism $k$.

source.place: Middle sentence: expand both composite restrictions on actions and arrows; identify them using the inverse-square equality.

proof.text: For every $M\in\Mod_S(\mathcal C)$ set $H_M=e_{a,\operatorname{Res}_\varphi M}^{-1}\circ k_M\circ\operatorname{Res}_\psi(e_{b,M})$. This has source $\operatorname{Res}_\psi\operatorname{Ext}_bM$ and target $\operatorname{Ext}_a\operatorname{Res}_\varphi M$, as checked in step 1. Its inverse is $\operatorname{Res}_\psi(e_{b,M}^{-1})\circ k_M^{-1}\circ e_{a,\operatorname{Res}_\varphi M}$; the two composites cancel to identities by functoriality and the inverse identities of the three factors. Put $L=\operatorname{Res}_\psi\circ\operatorname{Ext}_b$ and $T=\operatorname{Ext}_a\circ\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$. For $u\colon M\to N$, naturality of $e_a$, then of $k$, then of $e_b$ gives $T(u)\circ H_M=e_{a,\operatorname{Res}_\varphi N}^{-1}\circ(\operatorname{Res}_{a^{-1}}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi)(u)\circ k_M\circ\operatorname{Res}_\psi(e_{b,M})=e_{a,\operatorname{Res}_\varphi N}^{-1}\circ k_N\circ\operatorname{Res}_\psi(e_{b,N})\circ L(u)=H_N\circ L(u)$. This constructs the asserted natural isomorphism, rather than merely identifying its two functors up to unnamed comparisons.

source.place: Entire proof: compose the two extension comparisons with the identity comparison of the composite restrictions.
